search_log: Searched "Love the One You're With" "Emily Giffin" excerpt and opened the sustained preview on the author's official site.
Searched the title with "first person," narrator, and "point of view"; opened the Atlanta Journal-Constitution author interview explicitly identifying Ellen's first-person narration.
Checked the official Macmillan book page; its synopsis verifies the work and protagonist but does not independently state grammatical person.
Checked Google Books and a library-catalog excerpt; these supplied bibliographic confirmation or repeated opening material rather than additional whole-book structural evidence.
Searched for epistolary, multiple-narrator, frame, and alternating-POV evidence; found no credible indication of sustained narration in another person.
person_note: Ellen is the controlling participating narrator. Numerous event quotes from different parts of the story expose her narration through I, me, my, and mine, while the authorized opening independently shows the same first-person voice. The author interview further identifies Ellen as the narrator and explicitly describes the novel's first-person narration. The isolated he sentence is compatible with Ellen describing another character, and dialogue, aphorisms, and generic you passages are non-base evidence. No sustained contrary or alternating narrative person was found; the only residual limitation is that the authorized prose source covers the opening rather than the entire text, which is mitigated by the whole-book author interview and distributed quote evidence.
